name: US inflation
summary: US CPI about 4.1% a year in October and rising for three months; Fed officials discuss faster rate rises
state: The FRED CPI index puts annual US inflation at 4.08% in October, up from 4.02% in September and rising for a third month, inside the 3.0–4.5% Watch band (FRED). After the 10 Nov release, Fed officials including Dallas Fed President Logan and Governor Waller said on 10–11 Nov that price rises are broadening beyond energy and tariffs (BNN Bloomberg, 11 Nov). The November CPI report is due in mid-December.
for_you: Households on fixed incomes and those with variable-rate debt are most exposed to rising prices and higher borrowing costs. Wage growth below inflation reduces real incomes.
rubric_hit: CPI 4.08% y/y in Watch band 3.0–4.5% and rising 3 consecutive months; below 4.5% Alert line

sources.title: FRED — Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPIAUCSL)
BNN Bloomberg — US Fed officials consider faster hikes as higher prices seep into broader economy

why: Inflation sets Fed policy and thus global borrowing costs; a resurgence would keep rates high for everyone.
drivers: Energy, tariffs, wages, housing costs, supply chains.

rubric.watch: CPI 3.0–4.5%, or rising for 3 consecutive months.
